ideas.pitch: An AI-powered water resource management dashboard utilizing time-series forecasting to predict municipal reservoir stress and drought risk levels for Washington state water authorities.
ideas.title: AquaPredict WS
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the Water Resource Management theme of the hackathon with a heavy engineering backend that judges will favor over basic CRUD dashboards.

ideas.pitch: Satellite imagery analysis platform leveraging computer vision to monitor urban heat islands and unauthorized land clearing in smart city development zones.
ideas.title: EcoSat Urban Watch
ideas.why_it_could_win: Aligns with the Urban Intelligence and Climate themes while utilizing complex spatial intelligence similar to runner-up satellite monitoring hackathon projects.

ideas.pitch: A graph intelligence and machine learning platform that traces indirect corporate carbon emissions and supply chain climate risks in real-time.
ideas.title: CarbonGraph Climate Monitor
ideas.why_it_could_win: Combines graph intelligence with climate monitoring, borrowing architectural patterns from successful AML graph intelligence platforms.

ideas.pitch: An automated irrigation and groundwater depletion prediction system that uses multi-agent LLM reasoning to simulate agricultural water consumption under various climate scenarios.
ideas.title: HydroPulse AI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses Water Resource Management by combining predictive analytics with multi-agent orchestration, which performs well in hackathons.

ideas.pitch: A predictive urban air quality simulator that aggregates IoT sensor feeds to forecast localized pollution spikes and optimize smart traffic signal redirection.
ideas.title: SmartAir Urban Grid
ideas.why_it_could_win: Fits the Urban Intelligence track by offering a dual-purpose application that bridges environmental monitoring with smart city infrastructure.
